chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Abu Abdillah Yahya ibn Zakariyya ibn Shayban narrated to us, saying: Abu Sulayman Yusuf ibn Kulayb narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza narrated to us, from Sayf ibn Omayra, from Abu Bakr al-Hadhrami, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him) that he heard him say:

It is necessary that the Banu al-Abbas rule. When they rule, they will disagree and their affair will become scattered. Al-Khurasani and al-Sufyani will rise against them; one from the East and one from the West. They will race towards Kufa like two racehorses, one from here and one from here, until their destruction is at their hands. Indeed, they will not leave any of them alive forever.

key_terms.السُّفْيَانِيُّ: Al-Sufyani (a specific eschatological figure from Syria/Levant)
key_terms.الْخُرَاسَانِيُّ: Al-Khurasani (a specific eschatological figure from Khorasan)
key_terms.الْكُوفَةُ: Kufa (a major city in Iraq, significant in Shia eschatology)
key_terms.فَرَسَيْ رِهَانٍ: Two racehorses (metaphor for speed and rivalry)

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Baqir say about the fate of the Abbasids and the rise of al-Kurasani and al-Sufyani?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) outlines a specific eschatological sequence where the Abbasid caliphate, after establishing rule, succumbs to internal fragmentation, creating a vacuum for the rise of al-Khurasani from the East and al-Sufyani from the West. These two figures race to Kufa, engaging in a decisive conflict that results in the total eradication of the Abbasid lineage, a narrative deeply rooted in Shia historical expectations of political transition prior to the Mahdi's appearance.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (18) Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Sa’eed narrated from Abu Abdullah Yahya bin Zakariyya bin Shayban from Abu Sulayman Yousuf bin Kulayb from al-Hasan bin Ali bin Abu Hamza from Sayf bin Omayra from Abu Bakr al-Hadhrami that Abu Ja’far al-Baqir (as) had said:

“The Abbasids must rule. When they rule, they will disagree and their state will separate. Al-Khurasani and al-Sufyani will rise against them. One will come from the east and the other from the west. They will hurry towards Kufa as two racehorses. The decline of the Abbasids will be caused by these two leaders. None of them (the Abbasids) will remain alive.”
